items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: I worked with a guy up there called S. C. Henderson... I'd play along with him.

ctx.x: She says, "No, you're not. I'm going to call your dad and mother right now." She got on the phone and while she was on the phone, I had my clothes and they drove up and I just left with them, before she ever got them on the phone. So I left and went to Arkansas City and I worked with a guy up there called S. C. Henderson. Now he was an old-timer. See, and I'm just sort of getting, you know what I mean, and I learned a lot of tunes that -- he knew tunes that I didn't know, like we would get requests, but I would…

tunes that I didn't know, tunes like, 'This town is full of guys who think they mighty wise,' 'Ace in the Hole,' those kinds of tunes. So those were considered money tunes, you know? You know, certain tunes that these guys -- the gamblers would come in to hear, you know, and the other guys would come in to hear certain tunes. Well, we called them, they called them money tunes.
